parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the loop at lines 80-87. The loop reads a word with `inFile >> input`, then pushes the word, and immediately tests `if (inFile.eof()) break;`. For a normal file the extraction operator sets `eofbit` when it reaches the end of file (e.g., when the file is empty or when the last word has been read). Thus the `break` guarantees that the loop will terminate after the last successful read or after a failed read that has hit EOF. The only issue is that an empty string is pushed into `wordBank` when the file is empty, but this does not cause an infinite loop. The loop could only become infinite if the extraction fails without setting `eofbit`, which does not happen for the standard `>>` operator on `std::string` when reading from a file. Therefore the claim that the loop is prone to an infinite loop is incorrect.
